transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me?

Well... my wife thought I should come. It's mostly just... things going on at work. I do environmental modeling, and... well, I'm pretty sure the people on that contract have been tracking my revisions. 

They've been planting errors in the datasets. I think they're trying to make it look like I can't lead the work anymore. My wife, and the junior analysts at the office, they keep telling me it's just... you know, version-control mistakes. But... yeah. That's why I'm here.
How long have you been feeling that your coworkers are tampering with your data and trying to undermine you—days, weeks, or longer?

Well... longer than a few weeks. I suppose it's been... about two months now. That's when I knew for certain that they were tracking my revisions and... putting those errors in. Yeah. About two months.

Besides feeling that your coworkers are tampering with your data, have you noticed anything unusual with your senses—like hearing voices or sounds that others don't seem to hear, or seeing things that others don't see?
No... no, nothing like that. Just the data.

Before these last two months, would you say you were generally a trusting person, or have you always tended to suspect that others were trying to deceive or harm you, even going back to your teens or early adulthood?
I... no, I wouldn't say I've always been like that. I just... I do my work. I don't really know what you mean about my teens. I've always just kept to myself mostly.
Aside from the concerns about your coworkers, have you noticed any changes in how you're doing overall—at work, with your family, or in taking care of daily tasks?

I... well, I suppose work hasn't been going great. I've fallen a bit behind on the modeling deliverables. It got to the point where the firm... they actually reassigned pieces of the contract. And I guess I've stopped being much use to the junior analysts I'm supposed to supervise. I just... don't interact with them much right now. 

At home... I don't know. I mostly just keep to myself. My wife has had to... push me, I guess, just to keep basic routines going. That's all.
Have you noticed any changes in your emotions, like feeling less interested in things you used to enjoy, or finding it harder to show or feel emotions the way you used to?

I... I don't really know about emotions. I guess I just... don't do much anymore. 

I used to like things. Hiking... going to astronomy nights. Mentoring those younger analysts at work. But these days... I don't know. I can just sit at my desk, or out in the garage for hours. My telescope is out there, but... it just stays covered. I know I used to enjoy it, but I just don't feel any pull to uncover it. Or start anything. Or talk to anyone, really. That's all.

Did you notice yourself losing interest in things like hiking or astronomy and pulling away from people before you started suspecting your coworkers were tampering with your data, or did that start around the same time or after?
I... I'm not really sure. I don't keep track of the exact timeline. It's hard to say what happened first, or... I just don't really remember.

Thinking back, about how many weeks or months have you noticed this loss of interest and withdrawal—has it been roughly the same two months as the concerns about your coworkers, or did it start earlier or later?
I... I don't really keep track of the time. It's... it's all just sort of blurred together. I don't know exactly when it started. It's just... how it is now.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep or appetite over these past couple of months—like sleeping much more or less than usual, or a significant change in your eating?
I... I don't think so. I just sleep. And food... I eat whatever's around, I guess. I haven't really paid much attention to it.
Over these past couple of months, have you been feeling persistently sad, down, or hopeless, separate from your concerns about work?
I... no, I wouldn't say that. I'm not sad, exactly. Just... I don't know. I'm just trying to get by.

Have you or your wife noticed your thoughts feeling jumbled or hard to follow, or found yourself doing things that seemed odd or out of character to others, aside from the concerns about your coworkers?
No... I don't think so. My mind works fine. I just stick to my normal routine. If my wife thinks I'm doing something strange, she hasn't mentioned it to me.

When you think about not touching your telescope or not talking with the junior analysts, is that because you're worried it could be connected to the coworkers you suspect, or is it more that you just don't feel any desire to do those things regardless of that worry?

I don't think it's about being worried. I just... I don't know. I don't feel the pull to do much anymore. 

I can sit for hours at my desk, or out in the garage with the telescope still covered up. I know I used to enjoy things like that... going to astronomy nights, or hiking. Even mentoring those younger analysts. But now... I just don't have the desire to start anything. Or talk to anyone, really.

Before these past two months, going back further—say, three, four, or six months ago—had you already started pulling away from hobbies like hiking or astronomy, or was that withdrawal something that only began once the concerns about your coworkers started?

I... I don't really know. I haven't kept track of it like that. It's hard to say when exactly it started... whether it was three months ago or when. I'm just not sure if it was before or after. It's just how it is right now.

Since the exact timing is hard for you to pin down, would you be comfortable with me speaking to your wife about when she first noticed you pulling away from hobbies and people—was it more like six months ago, or closer to when the concerns about your coworkers started two months ago?
I suppose... if you need to talk to her, you can. She might remember better than I do. I don't really talk about it with her, though. But... yeah, if you want to ask her, that's fine.

patient.answer: No... I don't think so. My mind works fine. I just stick to my normal routine. If my wife thinks I'm doing something strange, she hasn't mentioned it to me.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient's loss of interest and withdrawal is a direct result of fear/suspicion related to the coworker delusion (consistent with delusional disorder) or a separate, primary loss of motivation/emotional flatness unrelated to the delusion (suggesting schizophrenia)
doctor.question: When you think about not touching your telescope or not talking with the junior analysts, is that because you're worried it could be connected to the coworkers you suspect, or is it more that you just don't feel any desire to do those things regardless of that worry?

target_item.name: Negative_Symptoms
target_item.manifestation: These days I can sit for hours at my desk or in the garage with the telescope still covered, knowing I used to enjoy hiking, mentoring the younger analysts, and going to astronomy nights, but I just don’t feel much pull to start anything or talk to anyone.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the lack of interest in previously enjoyed activities (like the telescope or talking with junior analysts) is due to a lack of desire/motivation or because of paranoid worries. This directly probes for negative symptoms (avolition/anhedonia) as opposed to secondary effects of delusions.

patient.answer:
I don't think it's about being worried. I just... I don't know. I don't feel the pull to do much anymore. 

I can sit for hours at my desk, or out in the garage with the telescope still covered up. I know I used to enjoy things like that... going to astronomy nights, or hiking. Even mentoring those younger analysts. But now... I just don't have the desire to start anything. Or talk to anyone, really.

inference.note: The patient's avolition and anhedonia appear independent of the delusional content (not explained by fear of coworkers), suggesting possible negative symptoms of schizophrenia rather than isolated delusional disorder; however, absence of hallucinations, thought disorder, or bizarre behavior keeps delusional disorder still plausible.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the negative symptoms (avolition, social withdrawal, anhedonia) and functional decline predate the 2-month delusional period, to assess if total symptom duration meets the 6-month threshold needed for a schizophrenia diagnosis versus a more circumscribed delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Before these past two months, going back further—say, three, four, or six months ago—had you already started pulling away from hobbies like hiking or astronomy, or was that withdrawal something that only began once the concerns about your coworkers started?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the timeline/onset of the negative symptoms (withdrawal from hobbies) relative to the psychotic symptoms (which started 2 months ago). patient.answer: I... I don't really know. I haven't kept track of it like that. It's hard to say when exactly it started... whether it was three months ago or when. I'm just not sure if it was before or after. It's just how it is right now.

inference.note: No new symptoms (hallucinations, disorganized speech, mood episode criteria) emerged to differentiate; persistent negative-symptom-like withdrawal and functional decline alongside encapsulated persecutory delusion keep both schizophrenia and delusional disorder viable. Unclear onset timeline of avolition relative to delusion prevents narrowing further.

doctor.intent: Clarify total duration of functional decline/negative symptoms (needed to meet the 6-month criterion for schizophrenia vs. a shorter course more consistent with delusional disorder), using collateral information since the patient cannot recall the timeline.
doctor.question: Since the exact timing is hard for you to pin down, would you be comfortable with me speaking to your wife about when she first noticed you pulling away from hobbies and people—was it more like six months ago, or closer to when the concerns about your coworkers started two months ago?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking for permission to speak with the patient's wife to clarify the timeline of the negative symptoms. There is no specific symptom profile item for granting permission to speak to a collateral informant.

patient.answer: I suppose... if you need to talk to her, you can. She might remember better than I do. I don't really talk about it with her, though. But... yeah, if you want to ask her, that's fine.

inference.note: The prominent negative symptoms (avolition, affective flattening, anhedonia, social withdrawal) alongside persecutory delusions and functional decline for over a month are inconsistent with delusional disorder (F22), which requires isolated delusions without such negative symptoms or marked personality/functional deterioration. This pattern better fits schizophrenia (F20.9), ruling out F22.
